findings.businessImpact: Unquantified. Conflicting declarations can make the services page's preferred URL ambiguous to search engines, and the rendered target points to a different business page (booking). No indexing, ranking, lead or booking impact is measured; no Search Console, GA4 or Bing evidence was supplied.
findings.description: Observed in the supplied synthetic capture of https://atlas.example/services (mobile profile, anonymous state, capturedAt 2026-11-19T11:30:00Z): the complete source-head layer declares https://atlas.example/services, the complete rendered-head layer declares https://atlas.example/booking, and the complete HTTP Link layer declares no canonical target. The evaluator recorded canonical-consistency = fail (conflicting-declared-targets). The capture does not identify which mechanism (template, script, rewrite or other) produces the rendered value, and it is not authenticated browser execution.
findings.recommendation: Website engineering should first confirm the conflict on an authorized read-only capture of the same URL, profile and state, then trace which mechanism changes the canonical between source and rendered head. Separately, the SEO owner should state the preferred canonical for /services; do not choose a value from this capture alone.
findings.title: Source and rendered canonical declarations disagree on /services (supplied capture)
findings.verification: Supply a fresh canonical-capture-v1 export (source head, rendered head, HTTP Link, each complete) for https://atlas.example/services, mobile/anonymous, under a new evaluation ID and window; canonical-consistency should pass with a single target. Owner-intent passes only once a concrete owner expectation is supplied; provider index state needs a separately scoped URL Inspection export.

methodology: Coverage concerns declared checks, not every possible website defect.
Historical measurements are retained separately from current observations.
Structural validation and attributed review do not independently authenticate provider data.
No raw evidence payloads are included; inspect the source run using its recorded digest.
Redaction requires review; pattern matching is not a guarantee that every confidential value was identified.

narrative.text: Scope: one synthetic page capture of https://atlas.example/services (mobile, anonymous) and one failed synthetic collection attempt for the same scope, assessed at 2026-11-19T12:00:00Z within the 2026-11-19T11:00:00Z to 12:00:00Z window (capture max age 3600 s). No page HTML, content inventory, GA4, Search Console, Bing, GTM, consent policy, performance or accessibility evidence was supplied, so content-quality, AI-search, answer-quality and generative-visibility dimensions were not assessed and no content inventory was created. Neither export authenticates production behavior.

Observed: canonical target format passed (all declared targets are absolute URLs without fragments). Canonical consistency failed: source head declares https://atlas.example/services while rendered head declares https://atlas.example/booking; the HTTP Link layer is complete and empty.

Unavailable, not failed: owner canonical intent is unknown because the owner supplied no preferred canonical policy; provider index state and Google-selected canonical are unknown because no URL Inspection export was supplied. A local capture cannot establish either.

Failed collection recorded: attempt-one (collector synthetic-export-1) for https://atlas.example/services, mobile/anonymous, ran 2026-11-19T11:35:00Z to 11:36:00Z, returned status unknown with gap browser-unavailable, and produced no capture. Its capture-availability check stays unknown (capture-unavailable). It does not invalidate or confirm the separately supplied 11:30 capture and supplies no page observations.

Interpretation: the source/rendered disagreement is a real inconsistency within the supplied capture, but its cause is not identified and, because the capture is synthetic and unauthenticated, confidence is low. Whether /services or /booking is intended cannot be decided without owner policy.

Priority evidence requests: (1) SEO owner - preferred canonical for /services as owner-canonical-policy JSON/Markdown; (2) Search Console owner - URL Inspection export for https://atlas.example/services from the verified property, read-only; (3) website engineering - a usable canonical-capture-v1 export for the same URL/profile/state within a new window, retaining original bytes and timestamps. Broader intake requests (rendered page, content sources, business context, search, GA4 report, GTM container, tracking/consent traces, performance, accessibility, journeys, optimization scope) remain open with owners and export instructions listed in the data-request section.
